terra.problem: Josiah being Jehoahaz’s father is a fact from outside the passage. The cited verse, 2 Kings 23:25, does not establish that relationship; 2 Kings 23:30 does.
Saying Jehoahaz stepped off Josiah’s road suggests he had previously followed it. The text does not say that.
Josiah being Jehoahaz’s father needs a reference outside the passage. The cited verse does not establish that relationship; 2 Kings 23:30 does.
Neco wanting the throne empty adds a motive the text does not give. It says Jehoahaz was imprisoned so he could not reign in Jerusalem.
The passage does not establish that there was no uniform or drilling, or describe a locked door.
Judah not getting a vote is not stated in the passage.
Calling Eliakim another son of Josiah relies on Jehoahaz also being Josiah’s son, a fact outside the passage that needs a reference such as 2 Kings 23:30.
The text says Neco made Eliakim king, but does not say nobody in Jerusalem handed out the crown.
Taking Jehoahaz home with him implies Neco personally traveled to Egypt with him. The text says Neco carried him off, but does not specify that detail.
No homecoming asserts that Jehoahaz never returned. The passage says he was carried to Egypt and died there, but does not address every intervening movement.
The passage does not say Jehoahaz never held the title of governor; it simply does not give him that role here.
The passage says Jehoahaz died in Egypt, but does not explicitly say he never returned to Jerusalem.
Saying Jehoahaz did not make it back to Judah goes beyond the passage, which says he was carried to Egypt and died there.
Saying the bill landed on everybody is broader than the text’s statement that Jehoiakim collected from the people according to each person’s wealth.
Neco wanting payment however it got collected adds an attitude the passage does not give him.
The explanation is mostly a plain restatement. Changing bosses offers a natural opening for Papa’s humor, but the line stays generic.
He stayed asserts a detail about Jehoiakim’s movements that the passage does not give.
Saying Jehoiakim served Nebuchadnezzar instead of hiding asserts that he did not hide. The passage does not address that.
Bringing in Gedaliah’s later governorship gives away a detail from later in this story group.
The passage does not say Shaphan stayed at his desk. Saying scribes keep records, not crowns, also makes a broader claim than the cited text establishes.
Saying the king of Egypt stayed home goes beyond the text, which says he did not march out of his land again.
Saying the king of Egypt stayed in his land goes beyond the text, which says he did not march out of it again.
Babylon holding the king of Egypt’s land can imply it held Egypt itself. The text specifies the territory taken from the Brook of Egypt to the Euphrates.
